title: 415 - Startropics
method: claude-code: written from the transcript, links verified by script

items.name: StarTropics
items.description: The episode's game: a 1990 Nintendo top-down adventure where Mike Jones throws a yo-yo through islands and dungeons.

items.name: StarTropics II: Zoda's Revenge
items.description: The 1994 sequel, which the hosts say they will reach very late in the show.

items.name: Nintendo Switch Online
items.description: The subscription service where hosts played StarTropics, which does not include the manual's code letter.

links.label: Wikipedia: Nintendo Classics
links.note: Line of classic Nintendo video games

items.name: Isekai
items.description: The anime and light novel genre where a person is transported into another world, compared to the game's opening.

links.label: Wikipedia: Isekai
links.note: Japanese fantasy subgenre about travel to another world

items.name: Doki Doki Literature Club!
items.description: The visual novel with a moment where it uses the player's real name.

items.name: The Legend of Zelda
items.description: The NES game StarTropics is most often compared to in look, dungeons and the yo-yo versus sword.

links.label: Wikipedia: The Legend of Zelda (video game)

items.name: Dragon Ball Z
items.description: Anime cited for characters named after foods, like Zoda and Cola names in this game.

links.label: Wikipedia: Dragon Ball Z
links.note: 1989–1996 television series based on the manga of the same name

items.name: Duck Hunt
items.description: One of the games in the NES compilation re-release the hosts mention at the start.

items.name: World Class Track Meet
items.description: One of the games in the NES compilation re-release the hosts mention.

items.name: NES Four Score
items.description: The four-player adapter that new NES releases are supporting.

links.label: Wikipedia: NES Four Score and Satellite

items.name: Mario
items.description: Compared as a human hero who was turned into more than a plumber; also joked as a lookalike mayor.

items.name: Chris Pratt
items.description: The actor who voiced Mario and is joked about voicing Link.

items.name: The Shawshank Redemption
items.description: Used as the example of a well-told story the hosts say StarTropics does not match.

items.name: Pokemon Red and Blue
items.description: The original Pokemon games, whose light story the hosts compare to StarTropics.

links.label: Wikipedia: Pokémon Red, Blue, and Yellow

items.name: Pokemon Legends: Arceus
items.description: A modern Pokemon game the hosts say is full of cutscenes.

items.name: Pokemon Legends: Z-A
items.description: The most recent Pokemon game the hosts say they watched as mostly text-heavy cutscenes.

items.name: Final Fantasy
items.description: Cited as a series with stories that reward thinking about what is going on.

items.name: The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword
items.description: Example of the linear Zelda era people complained about before Breath of the Wild.

links.label: Wikipedia: The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword

items.name: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild
items.description: The open Zelda game, whose heart gating for the Master Sword is compared to StarTropics's weapon upgrades.

links.label: Wikipedia: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild

items.name: Uncharted
items.description: A very linear modern series that one host compares StarTropics to.

items.name: The Witcher
items.description: Used as an open game one host also enjoys alongside linear ones.

items.name: Shohei Ohtani
items.description: Baseball star named as a pitcher who is also a good batter.

items.name: Rygar
items.description: The NES game whose weapon the hosts compare to the yo-yo.

items.name: Ratchet & Clank
items.description: Cited as an example of a 3D action game one host did not grow up on.

items.name: R.O.B.
items.description: The NES robot accessory that the sub's copilot looks like.

items.name: Big
items.description: The 1988 movie with the giant walkable piano that the game's piano puzzle recalls.

items.name: The Goonies
items.description: The adventure film with a piano that opens a door, which the game's pirate and piano puzzle evoke.

items.name: Metal Gear Solid
items.description: The other game known for needing a code printed on packaging, Meryl's codec frequency.

items.name: Hideo Kojima
items.description: Metal Gear Solid's designer, joked about in a discussion of who invented the packaging trick.

items.name: Snatcher
items.description: The Kojima game joked about as coming next.

links.label: Wikipedia: Snatcher (video game)
links.note: 1988 adventure game directed by Hideo Kojima

items.name: Wii Virtual Console
items.description: The service where the game's water-dunking code letter was recreated online.

links.label: Wikipedia: Virtual Console
links.note: Line of downloadable video games for several Nintendo platforms

items.name: Godzilla
items.description: Used to describe the chubby shape of Zoda's final form.

items.name: Contra
items.description: An NES game that turns into graphic alien imagery late, like StarTropics.

items.name: Wii Sports
items.description: The game whose Wiimote swing the fan sequel imitates.

items.name: EarthBound
items.description: Another Nintendo game with a baseball bat, a yo-yo and a normal kid, compared to StarTropics.

items.name: EarthBound Beginnings
items.description: The Famicom Mother game, which the show plans to cover on its Patreon.

items.name: Shin Megami Tensei
items.description: A Famicom-era franchise start the hosts plan to cover on their Patreon.

items.name: Castlevania
items.description: Subject of a ROM hack that removes knockback, used in the discussion of ROM hack improvements.

items.name: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim
items.description: Example of a game where someone might mod out the encumbrance system.

links.label: Wikipedia: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim

items.name: Dark Souls
items.description: Example of a game where someone might mod out losing souls on death.

items.description: The show's list of NES games that define the system; StarTropics was voted in.
